rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi moves from people whose animal-related subjection confirms resurrection to miraculous restoration, preservation, and origination; Job begins because bodily restoration through water epitomizes this sura's theme.
rows.anchor: ولما أتم سبحانه ذكر من سخر لهم العناصر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A reported genealogy makes Job a descendant of Isaac and Abraham and locates his estate in al-Bathniyya of Syria.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهو ابن أموص بن روم بن عيص بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had granted Job worldly prosperity; Job thanked Him, then endured his trial patiently.
rows.anchor: وكان الله قد بسط عليه الدنيا فشكره سبحانه ثم ابتاله فصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job says Satan's influence harmed his body, family, and possessions, and now threatened his religion.
rows.anchor: بتسليطك الشيطان علي في بدني وأهلي ومالي وقد طمع الآن في ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan prompted Job's wife to tell him to sacrifice an idol for a cure and then repent; Job recognized the temptation and vowed to strike her if cured, which distressed him.
rows.anchor: زين لامرأة أيوب عليه السلام أن تأمره أن يذبح الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complaining to God does not constitute impatience and therefore does not contradict Job's patience.
rows.anchor: والشكوى غلى الله تعالى ليست من الجزع فلا تنافي الصبر

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan says even complaining to people is compatible with patience when the complainant remains content with God's decree.
rows.anchor: سفيان بن عيينة : ولا من شكا إلى الناس وهو في شكواه راض بقضاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job alludes to a request for mercy without stating it directly, grounding his appeal in his need and God's supreme mercy; this subtlety makes the plea more likely to be answered.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعريض بسؤال الرحمة حيث ذكر نفسه بما يوجب الرحمة , وربه بأبلغ صفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's answer is described as if His response came into being at Job's call, highlighting divine greatness.
rows.anchor: اي أوجدنا إجابته إيجاد من كأنه طالب لها بسبب ندائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered Job to strike the ground with his foot; a spring emerged, and bathing in it restored his flesh and skin to exceptional health.
rows.anchor: بأن أمرناه أن يركض برجله , فتنبع له عين من ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restored Job's children and household after they had died.
rows.anchor: أحييناهم له بعد أن كانوا ماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi reads “with them” to show that the additional like-for-like family members were produced when Job's household was restored.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنهم وجدوا عند وجدان الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the gift mercy names the effect by its cause; “from Us” magnifies it and shows that only God could have bestowed it.
rows.anchor: وهو من تسمية المسبب باسم السبب , وفخمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job's story teaches worshippers to endure painful trials without assuming God despises them and to meet prosperity with gratitude lest it become their ruin.
rows.anchor: ليتأسوا به فيصبروا إذا ابتلوا بفتنة الضراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail was preserved as an infant through water by Gabriel's agency; Zamzam then remained lasting food and healing.
rows.anchor: سخرنا له من الماء بواسطة الروح الأمين ما عاش به صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an adult, Ismail was also preserved from being slaughtered: his father made every effort to obey God's command, but he was not killed by God's will.
rows.anchor: من الذبح فذبحه أبوه واجتهد في إتلافه امتثالا لأمرنا فلم ينذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris, son of Sheth and Adam, was brought back after death and raised to a high station; Biqaʿi calls him the first prophet sent among Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: أي ابن شيث بن آدم عليهم السلام الذي احييناه بعد موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says Dhu al-Kifl mastered sleep, the lesser death: he slept little, prayed through the night, fasted by day, judged people, and did not become angry.
rows.anchor: قدرناه على النوم الذي هو الموت الأصغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Kifl succeeded al-Yasa and undertook daytime fasting, nighttime prayer, and freedom from anger; mastering worldly life anticipates complete life in the next world.
rows.anchor: وهو خليفة اليسع عليه السلام تخلفه على أن يتكفل له بصيام النهار وقيام الليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view denies that Dhu al-Kifl was a prophet; this is opposed by al-Hasan's view that he was a prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه ليس ببني

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies Dhu al-Kifl as a prophet.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه نبي , وعن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Dhu al-Kifl as Ilyas.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه إلياس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification makes Dhu al-Kifl Yushaʿ ibn Nun.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported identification makes Dhu al-Kifl Zakariya.
rows.anchor: وقيل : زكريا - عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figures are grouped for their shared patience, then praised as those who receive the reward of the patient and are admitted to God's encompassing mercy.
rows.anchor: ولما قرن بينهم لهذه المناسبة , استأنف مدحهم فقال : { كل } أي كل واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are those formed for good who act according to that disposition and do whatever the Wise God approves.
rows.anchor: لكل ما يرضاه الحكيم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah left angry with his people and departed without waiting for God's specific permission to emigrate.
rows.anchor: اي على هيئة الغاضب لقومه بالهجرة عنهم , ولربه بالخروج عنهم دون الانتظار لإذن خاص منه بالهجرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Biqaʿi prefers al-Hasan's explanation that Jonah thought God would not punish him for this sin, a figurative expression of the consequence by its cause.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أن معنى { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه } أن لن نعاقبه بهذا الذنب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is reported to give the same explanation as al-Hasan: Jonah thought he would not be punished for his departure.
rows.anchor: رواه البهيقي في كتاب الأسماء والصفات عن قتادة عنه وعن مجاهد مثله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to explain the phrase as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
rows.anchor: من غير طريق عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An alternate report from Ibn Abbas through al-Asbahani explains the phrase as thinking God would not constrict his departure.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه , وكذا قال الأصبهاني عنه أن معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The constriction explanation derives from q-d-r meaning tightness, rather than q-d-r meaning ability.
rows.anchor: من القدر الذي معناه الضيق , لا من القدرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the verb has a doubled reading and can mean to decree or determine.
rows.anchor: وروى البهيقي أيضا عن الفراء نقدر بمعنى نقدر - مشددا وبحكم

rows.speaker: أبو صخر الهذلي
rows.claim: A line by Abu Sakhr al-Hudhali uses nقدر in support of the reported sense of determining or decreeing.
rows.anchor: وأنشد عن ابن الأنباري عن أبي صخر الهذلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admonished Jonah until he surrendered and cast himself into the sea; the whale swallowed him and descended to the sea floor, while God kept Jonah from becoming its food.
rows.anchor: فاقتضت حكمتنا أن عاتبناه حتى استسلم فألقى نفسه في البحر فالتقمه الحوت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir transmits from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and others that Jonah's darknesses were the whale's belly, the deep sea, and night.
rows.anchor: فهي ظلمات ثلاث - نقله ابن كثير عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما رضي الله عنهم

words: أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah first affirms God's exclusive divinity, then declares Him free of every imperfection; only God can rescue him from such a plight.
rows.anchor: أي تنزهت عن كل نقص , فلا يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah confesses that he wronged himself by leaving his people before permission and asks forgiveness, as a powerful person is expected to pardon.
rows.anchor: في خروجي من بين قومي فبل الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi links the answer to the report, “I am as My servant thinks of Me,” and says favorable hope requires continued remembrance and sincere recourse to God.
rows.anchor: تصديقا لظنه أن لن نعاقبه ( أنا عند ظن عبدي بي )

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says every person seeking refuge with God should begin with monotheism, then glorification and praise, then confession, seeking forgiveness, and apology; this is the proper order for every supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : وشرط كل من يلتجىء إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Jonah from distress by casting him onto the shore and shading him with a gourd tree; Biqaʿi presents rescue and deliverance as distinct favors.
rows.anchor: فألقاه الحوت على الساحل وأظله الله بشجرة القرع

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains the root sense of distress as a covering over the heart.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : وأصل الغم الغطاء على القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's rescue of Jonah signals that His honoring of prophets extends to their followers; since believers lack prophetic patience and face tests according to faith, God draws them gently from affliction.
rows.anchor: ما فعله من إكرام أنبيائه عام لأتباعهم بقوله : { وكذلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi cites the reports that prophets face the severest trials and that a person is tested according to their religion to explain believers' hardship.
rows.anchor: بما أشار إليه بحديث ( أشد الناس بلاء الأنبياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل )

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr from Asim read with a doubled jīm, explained as assimilation of the second nūn and as marking special care in the believers' rescue.
rows.anchor: قراءة ابن عامر وأبي بكر عن عاصم رضي الله عنه بتشديد الجيم لإدغام النون الثانية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the doubled form suggests that a believer who calls on God with Jonah's confession is rescued swiftly after a lapse, especially when discipline drives the believer back to God.
rows.anchor: فإن المؤمن متى حصلت له هفوة راجع ربه فنادى معترفا بذنبه هذا النداء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God folds the seven heavens and their inhabitants, and the seven earths and their inhabitants, in His right hand until all are like a mustard seed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : يطوي الله السماوات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is made intelligible by comparison with origination: both fall equally within God's power, which can restore what it created from its stores just as a lamp's light can be rekindled.
rows.anchor: دالا عليه مقربا له إلى العقول بتشبيه الإعادة بالإبداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite singular “first creation” distributes the claim over every kind of created thing, great or small, one by one.
rows.anchor: نكره ليفيد التفصيل واحدا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restores each thing in its corresponding state: gathers what was spread, revives the dead, reanimates what died, and returns people from the dust from which they began.
rows.anchor: فما كان متضام الأجزاء فمددناه نضمه بعد امتداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ability to create a thing in the first place entails that its creator can dispose of it in any way.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن من أوجد شيئا لا يبعد عليه التصرف فيه كيفما كان

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet preached that people will be gathered uncircumcised as they were first created; Abraham will be first clothed, and some of the Prophet's community will be taken leftward for innovations after his departure.
rows.anchor: خطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ( إنكم محشورون إلى الله غرلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling resurrection a promise, emphasizing that it rests on God, and affirming His enduring action stress both its certainty and the ease with which He does whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: أكد بقوله : { علينا } وزاده بقوله : { إنا كنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi connects the promise with the sura's recurring warning that wrongdoers are changed or punished while those who obey God are supported, citing its statements about God's knowledge and the earth's decline.
rows.anchor: حتى ختم بقوله { أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance promise resumes the connection to the earlier declaration that the revealed Book contains the community's reminder, and recalls God's promise through David.
rows.anchor: عاطفا على { لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur here is the scripture revealed to David; “after the reminder” means after the opening calls to God, admonitions, glorification, and praise that begin it.
rows.anchor: الذي أنزلناه على داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth” means the whole category of lands, including the worldly regions, the gathering place, Paradise, and other lands known to God.
rows.anchor: أي جنسها الشامل لبقاع أرض الدنيا كلها ولأرض المحشر والجنة وغير ذلك مما يعلمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their possessive link to God marks the servants' distinction; the righteous adopt the people of remembrance's character, turn to God, affirm His oneness, fear the Hour and His might, hope for His mercy, and humble themselves.
rows.anchor: أي المتخلفون بأخلاق أهل الذكر , المقبلين على ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets' stories in this sura witness that the final outcome belongs to those who please God.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن العاقبة لمن ارضانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi links the promise to Quranic assurances that God destroys oppressors and grants the land to chosen servants, and that believers inherit Paradise.
rows.anchor: إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise foretells that this comparatively weak community will inherit what David and Solomon received despite their great power over iron, wind, and animals of every kind.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إشارة بالبشارة بأنه تعالى يورث هذه الأمة على ضعفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi takes the promise in its apparent sense because the Zabur begins with remembrances and admonitions and repeats the same wording in Psalm 36 before its fourth section.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذا الكلام - والله أعلم - ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 1 depicts the righteous as avoiding the wicked, delighting in divine law and flourishing like a watered tree, while the wicked are chaff, fail in judgment, and perish.
rows.anchor: طوبى للرجل الذي لا يتبع رأي المنافقين , ولم يقف في طريق الخاطئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 2 describes nations and rulers conspiring against God and His anointed, God enthroning His king in Zion and promising him the nations and earth's ends, then warning rulers to serve Him and blessing those who trust Him.
rows.anchor: لماذا ارتجت الشعوب ؟ وهدت الأمم بالباطل ؟ قامت ملوك الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 5 presents a morning plea for an answer and guidance: God rejects evil and falsehood, while the speaker enters His temple through mercy and asks for a just path before enemies.
rows.anchor: استمع يارب قولي داعيا , وكن لدعائي مجيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 5 continues that God rejects hypocrites who anger Him, while those who trust Him rejoice, receive blessing, and are surrounded by His favor.
rows.anchor: ومثل كثرة نفاقهم ارفضهم لأنهم أسخطوك يا رب ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 6 pleads for mercy rather than angry rebuke, describes bodily pain and tearful nights, says the dead cannot praise God, and trusts that God has heard and will shame the enemies.
rows.anchor: يارب ! لا تبكتني بغضبك , ولا تؤدبني بزجرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 9 thanks God for wonders and for defeating enemies, destroying the wicked, and judging the world and its peoples with justice.
rows.anchor: أشكرك يا رب من كل قلبي , وأقص جميع عجائبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 12 laments feeling forgotten and threatened by enemies, but trusts God's mercy, rejoices in salvation, and promises to sing to Him.
rows.anchor: حتى متى يا رب تنساني ألى التمام ؟ حتى متى يارب تصرف وجهك عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 14 describes the one fit to dwell in God's sanctuary: blameless, truthful, harmless to neighbors, honoring the God-fearing, keeping promises, and refusing interest or bribes.
rows.anchor: يا رب من يسكن في مسكنك أو من يحل في طور قدسك ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 16 asks God to hear a just and truthful petitioner, who says God examined him without finding wrongdoing and asks protection from adversaries under God's wings.
rows.anchor: استمع يا الله ببري , وانظر إلى تواضعي , وأنصت لصلاتي من شفتين غير غاشتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 16 continues by asking God to rescue the speaker from hypocrites and enemy weapons and to scatter and divide the opponents.
rows.anchor: أدركهم وعرقلتهم , ونج نفسي من ا لمنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 17 praises God as strength and refuge: the speaker cries amid mortal danger, God hears from His temple, and earthquakes, fire, storm, thunder, and lightning accompany divine intervention.
rows.anchor: المزمور السابع عشر : أحبك يا رب قوتي ! الرب رجائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The psalm says God rescues the speaker from violent waters and stronger enemies, supports him, and brings him into spaciousness because He takes delight in him.
rows.anchor: أرسل من العلى وأخذني , نشلني من المياه الغزيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays the speaker according to his righteousness and clean hands; He is faithful to the pure and upright, acts against the crooked, saves the humble, and humbles the proud.
rows.anchor: جازاني الرب مثل بري , ومثل طهر يدي يعطيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lights the speaker's lamp, enables escape from ambush and passage over walls, and is perfect in His way; His tested word saves all who trust Him.
rows.anchor: وأنت يا رب تضيء سراجي , لأني بك أنجو من الرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God equips the speaker for battle, strengthens and raises him, gives victory over attackers, and leaves enemies unable to stand or obtain a rescuer.
rows.anchor: علم يدي القتال , شدد ذراعي مثل قوس نحاس , أعطاني الخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker asks rescue from hostile speech, becomes chief over peoples, and sees foreigners serve him; he praises God for deliverance and vengeance over his enemies.
rows.anchor: نجني من مقاومة الألسن , سيرني راسا على الشعوب
